searchText: **will_vill** A receipt would be async focused - although there may be situations in sync that a receipt could be used. It's a fairly general question though. For the most part, I hope smart contract developers don't have to think through things as receipt-driven. Goal is to have a lot of the underlying machinery be abstracted via HLLs like solidity or DSLs like vyper, etc. IE for a smart contract developer you can think through these problems within the model of asynchronous programming. quick question, the proposer does attest to its own block right? since the proposer is in the same committee as the attesters Yeah, the validator should perform any attestation duties as determined by its presence in a crosslink committee. It happens to be that block proposal leverages the crosslink committee shuffling so that every proposer for a slot also attests to the same slot; however we can imagine modifications to the proposer shuffling that change this relation For example something like private proposer selection Makes sense! excerpts.author: eth2_bridge_bot
excerpts.content:
**will_vill**
A receipt would be async focused - although there may be situations in sync that a receipt could be used. It's a fairly general question though. For the most part, I hope smart contract developers don't have to think through things as receipt-driven. Goal is to have a lot of the underlying machinery be abstracted via HLLs like solidity or DSLs like vyper, etc. IE for a smart contract developer you can think through these problems within the model of asynchronous programming.

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: quick question, the proposer does attest to its own block right? since the proposer is in the same committee as the attesters

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: Yeah, the validator should perform any attestation duties as determined by its presence in a crosslink committee. It happens to be that block proposal leverages the crosslink committee shuffling so that every proposer for a slot also attests to the same slot; however we can imagine modifications to the proposer shuffling that change this relation

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: For example something like private proposer selection
